methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Prusa Research, a bootstrapped manufacturer in the Robotics & Manufacturing sector, lacks sufficient comparable valuation anchors for conventional peer-based analysis. The identified comp universe consists of one public peer (ticker 277810.KQ) and eight private robotics firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. However, none of these peers share Prusa's stage, scale, or funding profile—all represent either later-stage venture-backed entities or public companies with substantially different capital structures.

The Peer-Median method was inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables. Screening the ten same-sector robotics peers yielded zero matches at identical stage, zero at adjacent stage, and zero in comparable valuation tier. A median derived from the full comp set would introduce material selection bias, as the public peer and all eight private comparables operate under different growth and liquidity constraints than a bootstrapped operation.

Without viable triangulation methods supported by the available data, this analysis cannot defensibly anchor a valuation range. Prusa's bootstrapped status and apparent focus on hardware manufacturing—distinct from the venture-scale automation and AI-robotics models of listed peers—creates a structural gap in the comp universe. Meaningful valuation would require either access to revenue or profitability metrics specific to Prusa, or identification of additional same-stage hardware manufacturers with disclosed valuations.
